claims.explanation: TWS-119 is a GSK3β inhibitor that activates canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling; sensitivity likely tracks with intact, active β-catenin signaling and dependence on Wnt/GSK3-regulated transcription, while resistance associates with PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT activation that bypasses GSK3 inhibition. The pattern of selective killing in EGFR-mutant NSCLC, squamous carcinomas, and CTNNB1/APC-mutant colorectal lines, versus protection in PTEN-mutant gliomas, breast, and thyroid lines, supports this axis.

features.basis: PTEN-mutant lines (BT549, U118MG, ZR751, FTC133, KALS1, SNU466, FTC238) are enriched among least affected, consistent with PI3K-AKT bypass of GSK3 inhibition
CTNNB1-mutant LOVO is selectively killed; Wnt/β-catenin activation is the drug's downstream axis
APC-mutant colorectal lines LOVO and SNUC5 are killed, linking Wnt pathway activation to sensitivity
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines HCC4006 and NCIH1650 are among most killed; EGFR signaling intersects GSK3/Wnt
BRAF-mutant lines NMCG1, RL952, SNUC5 appear in sensitive set, though BRAF-mutant melanomas are resistant, suggesting lineage context
NFE2L2-mutant squamous lines TE6, SNUC5, 253J are killed; oxidative stress response may interact with GSK3 inhibition
Most killed lines carry TP53 mutation, but this is near-universal in the panel and thus weak
Higher GSK3B expression may increase dependence on GSK3 activity, though direct target inhibition could also reduce sensitivity
MYC is an annotated target; MYC-driven lines may depend on GSK3-regulated MYC stability
JUN is an annotated target; AP-1 signaling via JUN may mediate sensitivity
PIK3CA-mutant lines SNU719, HT115, BT474 are among least affected, consistent with PI3K-AKT bypass
SMARCA4-mutant lines NCIH841, PLCPRF5, FTC238 are resistant, suggesting chromatin remodeling loss reduces dependence on GSK3/Wnt
